stories.title: One dead, homes swept away after Hurricane Lala lashes Hawaii
stories.summary: Hawaii is facing flash floods and mudslides that have swept away some homes after category one Hurricane Lala skirted Big Island, leaving one person dead in a car accident. A search-and-rescue operation was under way after several properties were uprooted from their foundations in the coastal communities of Naalehu and Waiohinu. Despite not even making landfall the storm still dumped to 35in (89cm) of rain in places, sending torrents raging down mountainsides. More than 200,000 householders were without power. Lala's eyewall howled past the Pacific US state without making landfall overnight before it was downgraded to a tropical storm. It is now moving westward, south of Hawaii. Tropical storm warnings remain in effect for all eight of Hawaii's major islands. Lala came within 30 miles (48km) of Big Island's South Point, but it was close enough to bring flash flooding, Hawaii County said on Sunday. The storm gained hurricane strength on Saturday afternoon, packing wind speeds of 91mph (147km/h). The National Hurricane Center (NHC) latest advisory at 14:00 EDT (18:00 GMT) on Sunday said Lala's winds had decreased to near 65mph. But the danger is not yet over. "Lala is expected to produce additional rainfall of 4 to 8 inches across the Big Island and windward Maui, with maximum storm totals of 30 to 35 inches," the NHC said, while the rest of the island chain could expect rainfall of 4 to 6in.

stories.title: Russian swimmers win bronze at 2026 European Aquatics Championships
stories.summary: British swimmers finished first, Italy was second
article_sentences: PARIS, August 16.
Russian swimmers won bronze at the 2026 European Aquatics Championships in Paris in the Women’s 4x100m Medley Relay event.
The Russian team of Alina Gaifutdinova, Yevgenia Chikunova, Darya Klepikova, and Kira Manyukhina covered the distance in 3 minutes and 53.79 seconds.
British swimmers finished first, setting the world record of 3 minutes and 53.50 seconds.
Italy was second (3 minutes and 53.60 seconds).
Russian athletes, who are competing in the neutral status, have won 31 medals at the tournament, including nine gold, nine silver, and 13 bronze medals.
The 2026 European Aquatics Championships is hosted by the French capital of Paris between July 31 and August 16 at the 5,000-seat capacity Paris Aquatic Center.
The tournament’s program in France includes competitions in Artistic Swimming, Diving, High Diving, Open Water and Swimming.
A total of 80 sets of medals are at stake across all competitions.
Russia is competing at the European Championships for the first time since 2021.
